g.text: First Principles (LHD/RHD), Corner Failure Modes, Rolle's, LMVT (Secant-Tangent Parallelism) & Cauchy's MVT
f(x) is differentiable at x = a iff Left Derivative equals Right Derivative as a finite number:
LHD and RHD exist, but LHD ≠ RHD.
Slopes diverge to ±∞ from opposite sides.
Derivative blows up to +∞ from both sides.
Converse is strictly FALSE! (|x| is cont, not diff).
Three Mandatory Hypotheses of Rolle's Theorem
CONCLUSION: ∃ at least one c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = 0 (Horizontal Tangent!)
• Between any two roots of a
AT LEAST ONE root of P'(x) = 0.
• If P'(x) = 0 has k real roots,
• TRAP: c must be strictly IN (a,b)!
If f(x) is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), then ∃ c ∈ (a, b) such that:
Physical meaning: Instantaneous rate of change at x = c EQUALS average rate of change over [a, b].
If m ≤ f'(x) ≤ M for all x ∈ (a, b):
m(b - a) ≤ f(b) - f(a) ≤ M(b - a)
• Prove: b - a < tan b - tan a
Ratio of Rates of Change Formulation
Let f(x), g(x) be continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), and g'(x) ≠ 0 in (a, b):
Special Case: When g(x) = x, CMVT simplifies directly to Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem!
CMVT provides the foundational proof of L'Hôpital's rule by choosing b = x and letting x ➔ a.
c = a or c = b is REJECTED.
Taylor expansion of f(x) about x = a with Lagrange form of remainder Rₙ(x):
When n = 1: f(x) = f(a) + f'(c)(x - a), which is precisely Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem!
LMVT is simply the 1st-degree Taylor polynomial with exact remainder.
TRAP 1: Forgetting that [a, b] continuity is REQUIRED for Rolle's & LMVT
If f(x) = 1/x on [-1, 1], f(-1) = -1, f(1) = 1. But f'(c) = -1/c² < 0 never equals 1! Fails because discontinuous at 0.
TRAP 2: Corner point invalidating Rolle's theorem
f(x) = 1 - |x| on [-1, 1]. f(-1) = 0 = f(1). Yet f'(x) = ±1 never vanishes. Fails because non-diff at x = 0.
TRAP 3: Accepting endpoints as roots for c
c MUST strictly lie in open interval (a, b). If algebraic solution yields c = a or c = b, it is an INVALID root!
TRAP 4: Misapplying L'Hôpital without verifying 0/0 or ∞/∞
lim_{x➔0} (x + 2)/(x + 1) = 2/1 = 2. Applying L'Hôpital gives 1/1 = 1 (WRONG!). Always check form first.
